sources.fact: MHCLG's official service provides domestic EPC, non-domestic EPC and DEC bulk CSV/API data for England and Wales; records from 2012 may include expired or replaced certificates.
Official guidance separates data dictionary, production method, methodology changes, limitations, licensing and API documentation.
Domestic, non-domestic and display-certificate CSV data dictionaries document variables, source and caveats.
The data can contain multiple EPCs/DECs for one building, including expired or replaced certificates.
The register does not contain every domestic/non-domestic/public building and must not be treated as a complete representation of building stock.
Official limitations identify invalid/no-data/not-recorded/null/extreme-value anomalies and place individual-building robustness responsibility on the assessor/accreditation scheme.
Excluded public data can include national-security cases, cancelled/not-for-issue certificates, opted-out buildings and specified Green Deal cases.
MHCLG states open address-level EPC data are updated monthly and, where possible, include UPRNs since November 2021.
The official register search supports postcode, street/town or certificate-number lookup for homes, business properties and public buildings.
A domestic EPC gives an A-G efficiency rating and is generally valid for 10 years; validity does not establish ownership or planning status.
Owners/occupiers may opt an EPC out of public disclosure; absence from public results is therefore not proof that no certificate exists.

The current private-rented-sector exemption register, published 5 May 2026, supports postcode/street/town searches for MEES exemptions and penalties; exemption status is distinct from planning viability.

examples.result: Where several EPCs exist, no arbitrary certificate is treated as current; validity/replacement chronology must be resolved.
UPRN is used as an addressable-location join key where present, not as a legal title or parcel polygon.
Missing EPC/open-data row is not treated as no-building/no-certificate because coverage and opt-out exclusions exist.
An EPC rating does not prove current occupancy, planning use class, redevelopment capacity or ownership.
NULL/invalid/not-recorded values remain missing/quality flags and are not imputed from nearby properties.
Non-domestic EPC floor/energy attributes are not converted into site area or residual land value.
MEES exemption/penalty records are regulatory evidence only and not a development-probability score.
No candidate promotion occurs from EPC/UPRN matching without exact HMLR title relation and current site-specific planning evidence.
